title: Injury to one limb can be read out from the opposite limb within 30 seconds

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Injury to one limb can be read out from the opposite limb within 30 seconds

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Limbs show mirror-neuron-like and somatotopic responses to injury outside the nervous system: the type and site of damage to one limb can be read out within 30 seconds by imaging the opposite, uninjured limb.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2022, Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds › Somatic Cognition: An Example of Unconventional Agency in Detail › Specific Parallels Between Morphogenesis and Basal Cognition

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: For example, mirror neurons and somatotopic representation are seen in limbs’ response to injury, where the type and site of damage to one limb can be read out within 30 s from imaging the opposite, un-injured limbs (Busse et al., 2018).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds”, Frontiers in systems neuroscience (2022), doi:10.3389/fnsys.2022.768201; section “Somatic Cognition: An Example of Unconventional Agency in Detail › Specific Parallels Between Morphogenesis and Basal Cognition”. Scope: Xenopus tadpole limbs (Busse et al., 2018)

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2022-tame-18: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.64

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Decoding injury from the opposite limb is an explicit and discriminating analysis. Published evidence can test the reported phenomenon, but raw imaging and controls needed for strong generalization may be incomplete.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Train and cross-validate a classifier to predict injury type and location from contralateral-limb imaging within 30 seconds, using held-out animals, sham injuries, and blocked neural or systemic signaling controls.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The mirror-neuron analogy exceeds the decoding result.

Raw time-resolved imaging may not be openly deposited.

Classifier leakage and animal-specific batch effects are risks.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.78
data adequacy: 0.38
analysis feasibility: 0.68
data existence: 0.48
operationalizability: 0.92

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The 2018 Xenopus study publishes correlations between stump geometry and the spatial extent of contralateral dye signal, which can be checked as a somatotopic association. The imaging window in that paper is dye incubation and a response on the order of an hour, and the images are not in a repository. The 30-second latency and the mirror-neuron description cannot be resolved from the published summaries.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Decode amputation level and injury type from images of the uninjured contralateral limb at 30 seconds, against sham and dye-only controls; readout holds if classification accuracy exceeds chance at that latency.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The published assay soaks tissue in voltage dye for about 30 minutes and reports depolarization by about one hour, so the 30-second clause is not in those summaries.

DiBAC fluorescence is not a pure membrane-voltage measurement, and the mirror-neuron wording is not a variable in the assay.

Images and animal-level measurements were not deposited.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

analysis feasibility: 0.35
discriminating power: 0.5
data adequacy: 0.4
